title: Function Pointer Syntax
concept: A function pointer stores the function address in a variable and changes the function to be executed at runtime.

steps.title: add function definition
steps.explanation:
`add` returns the addition of two integers.

The function name can be used like the function start address in a code area.

steps.title: sub function definition
steps.explanation:
`sub` performs subtraction with the same signature.

It has the same signature as `add`, so it can be connected to the same function pointer.

steps.title: Start main function
steps.explanation:
The main frame is created.

Now we declare a function pointer to make a replacement call to the target function.

steps.title: Function pointer declaration
steps.explanation:
`int (*op)(int, int)` is a function pointer that takes two ints and returns an int.

Be careful because if the parenthesis position changes, it will result in a completely different declaration.

steps.title: Address allocation for add function
steps.explanation: `op = add;` makes `op` point to the add function.

steps.title: Call add function through pointer
steps.explanation: The call `op(10,20)` is currently chained to add and returns result 30.

steps.title: Address reallocation of sub function
steps.explanation: Reassign another function address to the same pointer with `op = sub;`.

steps.title: Call sub function through pointer
steps.explanation: The same `op(10,20)` call, this time executing sub, returns -10.
steps.keyInsight: Even if the call expression is the same, the operation varies depending on the function pointed to by the pointer.

steps.title: Program exit
steps.explanation:
Exit with `return 0;`.

Bottom line: Function pointers are a tool for replacing execution targets at runtime.

quiz.question: void func(int x) What is the correct declaration of a pointer to a function?
quiz.explanation:
Return type must follow the format (*variable name)(parameter type).
The `(*p)` parentheses are key.

misconceptions.wrong: Function pointers have a different memory structure than variable pointers.
misconceptions.correct:
It is a variable that holds the same 32/64 bit address value.
It just points to the code area and not the data area.
misconceptions.why: From the CPU's perspective, both the data address and the code address are the same number.

keyTakeaway: Function pointers enable flexible design by allowing switching of functions to be executed at runtime.
